title.en: Essential elements, their roles and deficiency symptoms

heading.en: A plant needs more than water and light

hook.en: Paddy fields turn yellow without nitrogen; apples crack without boron; citrus leaves mottle without zinc. Plants need a short list of elements from the soil.

objectives.en: Explain hydroponics and the criteria for essentiality
Classify macro- and micronutrients and their roles

narration.en: Paddy fields turn yellow without nitrogen; apples crack without boron; citrus leaves mottle without zinc. Plants need a short list of elements from the soil.

body.en: An element is essential if (1) without it the plant cannot complete its life cycle, (2) its need is specific and cannot be met by another element, and (3) it is directly involved in metabolism. Hydroponics, in which plants grow in defined nutrient solutions, revealed 17 such elements. Macronutrients (more than 10 mmol/kg dry matter): C, H, O, N, P, K, S, Ca, Mg. Micronutrients: Fe, Mn, Cu, Mo, Zn, B, Cl, Ni. Elements may be structural (N, P, C), parts of energy compounds (Mg in chlorophyll, P in ATP), enzyme activators (Zn, Mg) or regulators of osmotic potential (K).

points.en: Macro: N P K S Ca Mg (+ C H O)
Micro: Fe Mn Cu Mo Zn B Cl Ni

title.en: The scarcest nutrient sets the growth

narration.en: Raise the supply of one nutrient while another is low: growth does not improve. The scarcest nutrient limits the plant.

caption.en: Set the supply of nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and iron as a percentage of the plant's need. Growth is limited by whichever is scarcest (critical concentration below 100%).

tryThis.en: Make nitrogen 30% and the rest 100%. What limits growth?
Now raise potassium to 200%. Does growth improve?
Iron is a micronutrient. Can it limit growth just as much?

title.en: Where do deficiency symptoms appear first?

say.en: Mobile elements are moved from old leaves to young ones.

text.en: Mobile: N, K, Mg  →  symptoms first in OLDER leaves

say.en: Immobile elements, part of structures, stay put.

text.en: Immobile: S, Ca  →  symptoms first in YOUNGER leaves

say.en: Common symptoms: chlorosis, necrosis, stunting, delayed flowering.

text.en: Chlorosis: N, K, Mg, S, Fe, Mn, Zn, Mo
Inhibited cell division: N, K, S, Mo

caption.en: Optional: magnesium sits in the chlorophyll of the chloroplasts; calcium is in the middle lamella of the cell wall; potassium keeps the vacuole's osmotic balance.

problem.en: A plant shows yellowing between the veins of its YOUNGEST leaves while older leaves stay green. Which elements are likely deficient and why?

steps.en: Symptoms on young leaves point to an immobile element.
Interveinal chlorosis of young leaves is typical of iron (also sulphur, calcium among immobile ones).
Iron is needed to make chlorophyll and is not remobilised.

points.en: Essential elements: needed to complete the life cycle, specific, directly involved in metabolism.
Macronutrients: C H O N P K S Ca Mg; micronutrients: Fe Mn Cu Mo Zn B Cl Ni.
Mobile elements show deficiency in old leaves, immobile ones in young leaves; toxicity of one can cause deficiency of others.
